title: Jala and the Returning Voice
logline: Jala calls into the world and learns that every voice comes home.
story: At the rim of the great valley where Wisal, who was union with the beloved, was said to dwell, Jala — carrying clearness after rain — shouted a harsh word into the dark, and a harsh word came back; then Jala shouted a kind one, and kindness returned. For a long while Jala only listened to the echoes, learning their quiet law. By dusk Jala understood that the valley had never invented a single sound — it had only returned what was given. Jala walked home speaking gently, knowing the world was an honest mirror.
moral: Whatever you send into the world returns to you; the world keeps no other ledger.
